core_job: For singer-songwriters and hobby guitarists or pianists: write a song as a chord chart (sections, bars, chords, lyrics), press Play and hear a band play exactly those chords, record voice or instrument takes over it inside the song, and share a demo audio file and a chord sheet. Everything stays on the device, with no account.
signature: The Chart Band. Each section is a row of bar cells. Tapping a bar opens a chord palette for the section's key (diatonic chords as roman numerals and names), plus quality and slash-bass entry and fills from common progressions. The sequencer then plays the chord of each bar: bass on the root and fifth, a comp instrument the user picks on the chord tones, and drums in the chosen groove. Today it plays only the key's triad. The whole song can be transposed in one tap. The song can be bounced offline in an isolate into one WAV (band plus unmuted WAV takes) and exported as a plain-text chord and lyric sheet. It is built only from on-device Dart chord theory and the existing Dart PCM synthesis. GarageBand is partially verified as lacking this: four Apple guide and App Store pages fetched with curl show that sections start empty and are filled by recording, chords are performed on chord strips, and the only lyrics space is one Note Pad per song. Chord-chart apps such as iReal Pro and Chordbot: competitor not verified, because web search is disabled.
must: M1 Songs become real projects. Song and Section models are saved as one JSON file per song in Application Support with atomic writes. Users can create, rename, duplicate and delete songs, and edit each section's key, bar count, chords and lyrics. Old tracks, drum pattern and recordings are migrated once. A fresh install starts with an empty library: kDefaultTracks no longer seeds it.

M2 Build the Chart Band. A tested chord parser and speller, a diatonic palette per key and progression fills. The sequencer plays the chord of each bar, including split bars, rests and loop-section. Tempo with tap tempo, groove, comp instrument and transpose are saved per song.

M3 Takes are recorded inside the song over the band: a 1-bar count-in, an always-visible headphones hint, and WAV PCM16 44.1 kHz files stored under songs/<id>/takes. Each take records its start section, latency nudge, gain and mute, and can be renamed, deleted or shared. States are handled for mic denied (with Open Settings), interruptions and missing files. Recording over playback must be checked on a physical iPhone. No take can exist outside a song; this is the AGRecorder boundary.
M4 Share and export. A plain-text chord and lyric sheet in a fixed, tested format, and a bounced demo WAV (band plus unmuted takes) rendered in an isolate with progress and Cancel, using share_plus.

M5 Depth. The Songs library is the home screen. Search covers title, lyrics and chord symbols. Filters: All, Has takes, No chords yet. Sort: Recently edited or A-Z. Real empty states for the library and for a section with no chords, error states for a corrupt song file or an unreadable library, and an explicit note that there is no offline state because the core job never uses the network.

M6 Its own identity. Palette 'rehearsal room': walnut #1E1A17, surface #2A2420, ivory #F2E8D5, brass seed #B8862B, felt-red #9E2B25 for record, plus section colours; rg found 0 uses of these hexes in any app. Fonts are bundled Work Sans and Barlow Condensed SemiBold (OFL, HTTP 200, 0 uses in other apps). Lead-sheet shapes with a 6 dp radius and no emoji used as icons. Home is library, then chart screen, with a bottom transport dock and no NavigationBar-plus-banner shell. A one-screen onboarding, 'Your chords, played by a band.', with a 'Write a song' button. New Settings copy, a hand-drawn icon, a launch screen whose storyboard sha differs from 3f6a9b27d8, and CFBundleDisplayName 'VirtuBand' (today 'Virtuband').

M7 Remove template tells and dead surfaces: the AI Compose screen and the unused AI_ENDPOINT, AI_API_KEY and JAM_SERVER_URL config; Dashboard; Notifications; Jam (folded into the song); Recordings (replaced by takes inside songs); the optional Supabase sign-in with app_env, supabase_config and auth_service (founder question 1); the Push and Affiliate mocks, including the Amazon tag virtuband-20; 'Get Started'; the 'Virtual Music Studio' tagline; '· Flutter'; and every Tailwind hex.

M8 Honest and 5.6-safe. No seeded songs or takes. Reviewers get no login, no demo mode and no detection. No long-press-only paths: the instrument grid is reachable only by long-press today, and the review notes point Apple to it. No Remote Config reads (enforced by a test). The banner shows only on the Songs library. Remove the interstitial fired after each saved take.

M9 Proven. flutter analyze is clean. All tests pass with a count of at least 224 (the baseline, measured this session), and new tests cover the parser, palette, transpose, sequencer, song JSON, migration, take placement, bounce mixer, chord-sheet format, search, onboarding, the tell guard and layout. Tests of deleted screens are replaced, and each replacement is listed in the commit message. The screenshot integration test is rewritten. Commits are path-limited, never touching fastlane/ or the pbxproj that other people have modified, and pushed to main. The developer launches the app on a simulator and takes screenshots.
